title: OpenWQ: Open Water Quality modeling framework
description:
OpenWQ (Open Water Quality) is a model-agnostic, multi-chemistry biogeochemical framework written in C++ that extends existing hydrological and Earth system models with flexible water-quality simulation. It couples to host models (e.g., SUMMA, mizuRoute, CRHM) through a model-agnostic API and lightweight host-specific couplers, separating process representations from the numerical solver. Interchangeable modules cover dissolved transport, user-defined biogeochemical reaction networks (and PHREEQC geochemistry), sediment transport, lateral exchange, and sorption, all configured through JSON files. The release includes the Python supporting scripts for model configuration, land-cover-based nutrient loading, observation retrieval from GRQA, calibration (DDS), and post-processing.

This is the version used in Costa et al. (submitted to the Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems).

Documentation: https://openwq.readthedocs.io/ — Getting started: https://ue-hydro.uevora.pt/ue-hydro-models/
